answer:
Yes. NovaLearn should keep Advanced OCR Pipeline work ahead of the Microsoft Teams integration.

- The corpus explicitly identifies the Advanced OCR Pipeline as the company’s “highest technical priority,” with release scheduled for August 2026 [NL-001#NL-001-S08].
- Scanned PDFs are the primary driver of citation errors and onboarding delays; in May, 27% of support tickets related to import issues and broken citations from scanned PDFs [NL-015#NL-015-S06].
- The CTO argues OCR is a “critical system stability requirement,” while rushing Teams would require a complete auth-layer redesign and risk tenant-isolation breaches [NL-015#NL-015-S06].
- Product leadership agrees that delivering a Teams integration before fixing ingestion would only spread inaccurate, uncited answers to a larger audience; OCR must remain top priority, with Teams staying in design phase for Q4 2026 and development in early 2027 [NL-015#NL-015-S06].
- Official talk tracks also point to the OCR pipeline launching in August 2026 and the Teams integration being designed from the ground up for permission enforcement, scheduled for Q4 2026 [NL-032#NL-032-S05].
- Teams is in high demand, but the roadmap places it in design phase for Q4 2026, while WorkflowCoach and other items are also competing for engineering time [NL-011#NL-011-S07].

Business recommendation: prioritize OCR first because accurate ingestion and citation grounding are prerequisites for any secure, trustworthy Teams deployment. Launching Teams prematurely would expose users to broken citations and unauthorized-data risks, undermining the enterprise security and accuracy value proposition NovaLearn sells against competitors [NL-015#NL-015-S06] [NL-032#NL-032-S02].
